prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right choice depends on your budget, preferred insurers, whether you want in‑person help, and whether you need assistance with ACA subsidies, HSA plans, or a small‑group (SHOP) policy for employees. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best broker in Kansas City, MO plus a few reputable places to start.

How to pick a great broker for a self‑employed person
- Look for an independent agent/broker (not captive to one insurer) so you get quotes from multiple carriers.  
- Make sure they are certified to sell ACA/Marketplace plans if you want subsidy help.  
- Prefer brokers who regularly serve self‑employed / gig workers and understand the self‑employed health insurance deduction and how income affects subsidies.  
- Ask about fees — most individual-market brokers are paid by insurers, but confirm there are no surprise fees.  
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp), licensing with the Missouri Department of Insurance, and membership in professional groups (NAHU).  

Good places/resources to search
- Healthcare.gov broker/assister finder or the Missouri marketplace portal — for brokers certified to enroll people in Marketplace plans and subsidies.  
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” tool — shows licensed local agents.  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — to verify licenses and complaints.  
- Local small‑business resources: Kansas City SBDC or Chamber of Commerce can recommend brokers who work with microbusinesses and independent contractors.  
- Online brokers/marketplaces (if you prefer a digital experience): eHealth, HealthSherpa, GoHealth — they compare multiple plans quickly and can assist with Marketplace enrollments.

Questions to ask any broker before you sign up
- Which insurers/plans do you work with locally in Kansas City?  
- Do you help with Marketplace enrollment and subsidy calculations?  
- Will you assist with claims and renewals next year?  
- How do you get paid? Any client fees?  
- Can you show sample networks (doctors/hospitals) for plans I’m considering (especially if you use KU Med, Saint Luke’s, Children’s Mercy, etc.)?  
- Do you have experience helping self‑employed people who file Schedule C?  

Next step
If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether you prefer in‑person help or online/phone only, and I’ll look up and suggest several local brokers or agencies in Kansas City with good reputations and the right experience.
